title: Słuchanie – 6 wypowiedzi (syntezator mowy)
intro: Posłuchaj każdej wypowiedzi dwa razy i wybierz odpowiedź.

items.prompt: What does the woman say about her reasons for volunteering?
options: She began for practical reasons, but her motivation changed.
She was asked by her teacher to help.
She has always wanted to work with animals.
items.explanation: Zaczęła dla CV, potem motywacja się zmieniła.
items.script:
Interviewer: You've been a volunteer at the animal shelter for three years. What made you start?
Woman: Honestly, I wanted something to put on my CV. But after the first week I realised that it was about much more than that. Now I go there every Saturday, even when I have an exam on Monday.

items.prompt: What is the man's opinion about learning languages?
options: Grammar is the most important thing.
Speaking with real people is the fastest way.
Word lists are enough for beginners.
items.explanation: Mówienie z ludźmi dało największy postęp.
items.script: Man: I used to think that learning a language meant memorising word lists. Then I spent a summer in Spain and nobody cared about my grammar, they just wanted me to talk. It was terrifying at first, but my Spanish improved more in two months than in two years at school.

items.prompt: What do the shop owners fear?
items.script: Woman: Our city is introducing a new rule: cars will not be allowed in the town centre on Sundays. Some shop owners are afraid that they will lose customers. However, research from other cities suggests that the opposite happens, because more people walk and stay longer.

items.prompt: What does the speaker think of the film?
options: He doesn't recommend it at all.
He has mixed feelings about it.
He thinks the ending was the best part.
items.explanation: Opinia mieszana: słaba końcówka, świetna muzyka.
items.script: Man: I'd say the film was a bit disappointing. The story started well, but the ending was very predictable. Having said that, the music was fantastic and the actors did a great job, so I wouldn't tell people to avoid it.

items.prompt: How is the speaker's approach to resolutions different this year?
items.script: Woman: Every year I make a list of resolutions, and every year I give up by February. This time I'm doing it differently. Instead of big goals like 'get fit', I set tiny ones, for instance, 'walk for ten minutes after dinner'. So far it's working.

options: Working from home is too expensive.
items.script: Man: The company's new policy allows employees to work from home two days a week. My manager says it will save money on office space. Personally, I'm not sure. I think teamwork suffers when people don't see each other regularly.
